population: Iranian; 227 community-dwelling adults aged 60-90, Birjand Longitudinal Aging Study
conclusion: No significant association between the rs117385980 T allele and frailty. A non-significant trend toward absence of the T allele in the oldest band: 1.39% at 60-69, 4.65% at 70-79, 0% at 80-90 (Fisher exact p=0.073).
study_design: case-control nested in a community cohort; exploratory, PCR-RFLP genotyping
provenance_quote: However, a non-significant trend was observed, suggesting a potential inverse relationship between the T allele and advanced age, which may imply a role in longevity.
